# OzDDNS

> OzDDNS is a provider-centric, self-hosted dynamic DNS manager distributed as a single Go binary. It discovers the current address, reads the live DNS record, and writes only when the desired state differs. The binary embeds a Vue web panel, REST API, CLI, scheduler, and SQLite storage.

- Version: 2.0.3
- Homepage: https://ozddns.pages.dev/
- Source: https://github.com/echoface/ozddns
- Container image: ghcr.io/echoface/ozddns
- Default bind: 127.0.0.1:9876
- Runtime: Go 1.26+, one process, SQLite
- License: no license file yet; source-available, not open source

## Core behavior

- Address sources: HTTP endpoint, local network interface, shell command, and static value.
- Reconciliation: read the live record, diff it, and write only when it differs. Dry runs are available from the panel, CLI, and API.
- Scheduling: per-task intervals with jitter, concurrency limits, and rolling execution history.
- Surfaces: the embedded Vue panel, REST API, and CLI share the same application layer.
- Storage: SQLite, with configuration export/import and webhook notifications.

## Supported providers

Cloudflare, Alibaba Cloud DNS (alidns), DNSPod, DuckDNS, Namecheap, GoDaddy, deSEC, Vercel DNS, and custom HTTP endpoints. A and AAAA records are supported where the provider allows them. Cloudflare records can carry proxy state.

## Deployment

- Run the published multi-arch container image (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) or build the binary from source.
- One `ozddns serve` process owns HTTP, scheduling, reconciliation, and SQLite. systemd or Docker supervises that single process.
- Default panel address: `http://127.0.0.1:9876/`.
- OzDDNS does not terminate TLS; use a trusted reverse proxy.

## Security model

- Targets a trusted single-user machine.
- Open mode is only appropriate on loopback. Exposure beyond loopback without authorization is warned in the CLI and UI.
- Authorization is opt-in: password, TOTP or single-use recovery code, then an opaque server-side session.
- First authorization setup is accepted only from loopback.
- Provider credentials are masked in ordinary reads; exports contain them and must be protected.
- `trustProxy` is only for deployments where a trusted proxy overwrites `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-For`.
